q: what is the relationship between bees and flowers
a: A flower is the reproductive structure of flowering plants (angiosperms). Its main parts are the petals (often colorful to attract pollinators), the sepals (protective outer parts), the stamen (male part producing pollen), and the pistil (female part containing the ovary). Flowers attract pollinators like bees, butterflies, birds, and bats using color, scent, and nectar. When a bee visits a flower for nectar, pollen sticks to its body and is carried to the next flower, fertilizing it — this process, called pollination, is how most flowering plants reproduce and produce fruits and seeds. The relationship between bees and flowers is one of the great mutualisms of nature: flowers get pollinated and bees get food. Roughly 75-80% of flowering plants depend on animal pollinators, and bees are the most important of them.
